claims.text: Spin-polarized DFT with DFT+U or hybrid functionals can correctly predict ferromagnetic ground states when spin polarization and exchange interactions are essential.
A ferromagnetic ground state is indicated when the ferromagnetic configuration has lower total energy than non-magnetic and antiferromagnetic alternatives.
The material is initially non-magnetic or weakly magnetic and has no pre-imposed spin ordering.
Advanced spin-polarized exchange-correlation treatments can resolve spin polarization and subtle energy differences among competing magnetic orders.
Calculations at approximately 0 K effectively represent ground-state magnetic ordering.
The electronic structure and local atomic environment facilitate exchange interactions that are critical for ferromagnetic ordering.
Including spin polarization allows a calculation to capture exchange splitting.
DFT+U or hybrid treatments can capture electron-correlation effects relevant to magnetic ordering.
Capturing exchange splitting and correlation effects lowers the calculated energy of the ferromagnetic configuration when it is the true ground state.
The computed ferromagnetic state will have lower total energy than competing non-magnetic or antiferromagnetic states.
Non-spin-polarized DFT does not explicitly account for exchange splitting.
Non-spin-polarized DFT may fail to resolve subtle energy differences among competing magnetic states.
The proposed approach is expected to be effective for systems with moderate electronic-correlation effects.
Strongly correlated systems may require adjustments beyond the stated advanced functionals to capture magnetic behavior reliably.
Predicted magnetic energy differences and the robustness of ferromagnetic ordering depend on material-specific parameters.
Predictions can depend on the selected U value or fraction of exact exchange.
Experimental verification is required to confirm the computational prediction.
